Newbie question, but I know to frequent opening lets the humidity out. How often should I check the water level? Thanks.
How often should I check the distilled water level in the Humidor? How often do you have to add water?
What kind of humidification system are you using atm?
In my regular humidor, I have a disc you fill with distilled water, and a monitor. In my overflow tupperdor, I have a small bowel of distilled water in the tupperware container.

Ok, trash all of that. Order some Boveda's (suuuper cheap, like $1-3 per packet IIRC) and they can last you a looooooong time.

Bovedas are a two way RH system, this means that not only will the Boveda pack get your RH to where you want it (the % is listed on the item) but it will also absorb and hold more than it should to regulate and keep the RH stable. You can alway re-charge bovedas by simply submerging them into water and sealing them up for a day or so, let them air dry over-night and re-use!

You can see the boveda is not working once it starts to become hard, then you just re-fill!

I definitely agree with /u/CaveJohnson. Those humidification methods are notorious for mold growth. Get a couple of large 65% or 69% Boveda packs (you should use 1 + 1 for every 25 cigars in your humidor, so if you have 100 cigars in a humidor I'd use 5 boveda packs).

Feel free to let us know if you have any other questions.
They came today, and they are great.
Wait, you can re-charge them? I have a coupe I was about to replace, I'll give them a soak in distilled water. Thanks!

Bovedas are the way to go. They offer two way humidification control so that if your ambient humidity goes above what is listed on the pack, it will absorb water and keep things stable. Discs or a bowel of water can only add more water to the air. This is a problem if you do not control temperatures VERY tightly.

I really like the heartfelt beads as they are almost fool proof. The best way to take care of cigars honestly is to have a digital hygro. When it reads lower or higher RH than you want then you know its time to make some changes.

I'm anal about checking mine every day, so I have a few drops in a stainless shot glass. My digital monitor tells me when it's 68% (my target). I usually have to refill it about every four to five days in this weather. The other methods are much more precise, though.
